label: Run BEFORE StudySS2 data exists, on CODA-LM Val reference answers fetched directly (Apache-2.0, ungated, KaiChen1998/coda-lm). 25 scenes x 3 tasks = 75 identity pairs.
design: IDENTITY CONTROL: the reference answer is submitted as the PREDICTION against itself. The reference is the gold standard by construction, so an identity pair must sit at the top of the 1-10 scale. CLAUDE.md check 7: a known-good input must pass the check being applied, and if it fails the CHECK is broken rather than the arm.
why_the_paper_cannot_supply_this_anchor: arXiv:2404.10595 section 4.2 records HUMAN VERIFICATION of the GPT-4 evaluations before its Table 2 numbers, so its published Text-Scores cannot calibrate our unverified pipeline. With no valid external comparator there would be no anchor for the absolute level at all.

RESULT.verdict: PASS, and at the ceiling: ALL 75 identity pairs scored EXACTLY 10.0, with no variance at all.

what_this_buys.outcome_realised: the first of the three anticipated outcomes: references score 9 to 10, so THE TOP OF THE SCALE IS ANCHORED.
what_this_buys.consequence: a model answer scoring 7 can be read as genuinely below reference quality rather than as an artefact of a judge that never awards high marks. Absolute levels on CODA-LM become PARTIALLY interpretable, which is more than EgoThink has.
what_this_buys.what_it_does_not_establish: that the judge discriminates WELL between non-identical answers of differing quality. An identity pair is the easiest possible case; a ceiling at 10.0 with zero variance is consistent both with a well-calibrated judge and with one that rewards verbatim overlap. The real run supplies that evidence, not this control.

parser_validated_on_LIVE_output.note: the new 1-10 parser is now validated against live judge output rather than only the 18 self-test vectors, and the reason codes were exercised. 0 out-of-range, so the judge complied with the 1-10 format on every call.

A_THIRD_FINDING_MY_OWN_GATE_FAILED_FOR_T.what: the parser gate reported parse_rate 0.6667 and FAIL, with 25 of 75 as no_match.
A_THIRD_FINDING_MY_OWN_GATE_FAILED_FOR_T.cause: I ran the gate on a STORED EXCERPT truncated to 300 characters, not on the text the parser saw. CODA-LM judges write their short explanation FIRST and the rating LAST, so a head truncation drops the rating entirely: 31 of 75 responses exceeded 300 characters and 25 of those lose their rating to the cut.
A_THIRD_FINDING_MY_OWN_GATE_FAILED_FOR_T.lesson: a coverage gate must be fed the text the parser actually consumed. Mine measured a different string and returned a confident FAIL on a parser that was working perfectly, which is the mirror of the StudySS1 failure: there a broken parser reported a working mean, here a working parser got a broken gate.
A_THIRD_FINDING_MY_OWN_GATE_FAILED_FOR_T.does_this_affect_StudySS1: NO. SS1 parsed at call time on the full response and only then truncated judge_raw for storage, so its unparsed counts are real. The EgoThink missingness analysis likewise used the call-time judge_rating rather than re-parsing stored text. Only a RE-analysis from stored output would be affected, and none was done.
A_THIRD_FINDING_MY_OWN_GATE_FAILED_FOR_T.forward_rule: store enough of the response to re-parse it, or store the parsed value and the reason beside the excerpt. The excerpt is not a substitute for the input.

prompts_are_verbatim.mapping: stage1 -> general (few-shot scene_few_shot), stage2 -> suggestion (few-shot suggestion_few_shot), stage3 -> regional (no few-shot)
prompts_are_verbatim.all_three_instruct_the_judge_to_ignore_l: "Do not allow the length of the predicted text to influence your evaluation." present in all three system prompts.
prompts_are_verbatim.consequence_for_carryover_7: the within-model length-tercile check on CODA-LM is therefore not a re-measurement of the EgoThink length bias; it tests whether an EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION to ignore length works on a 7B judge. A length effect here is a failure to follow an instruction, which is a stronger finding than an unprompted bias.

split_caveat: these references are CODA-LM Val, fetched directly. If the StudySS2 producer stages a different split or subset, this anchor is measured on different text than the run it anchors, and must be re-run against the staged references. Recorded so a mismatch is detectable rather than assumed absent.
